one_liner: C HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 server inside PHP (TrueAsync fork) that out-runs HttpArena's nginx on small-response HTTP/2.
what_it_does: A PHP extension (C core on llhttp, nghttp2, ngtcp2/nghttp3 and the TrueAsync libuv reactor) that runs the whole web server inside the PHP process: no FastCGI, php-fpm or reverse proxy. You build an HttpServerConfig (listeners, TLS, workers, compression), register PHP callbacks with addHttpHandler / addGrpcHandler / addWebSocketHandler, mount a C StaticHandler for files, and call start(). It is not a drop-in for nginx: it is an application server for PHP code, and it only runs on the TrueAsync fork of PHP 8.6.
how_it_is_fast: One libuv event loop per worker thread (setWorkers(N) spawns an Async\ThreadPool), each binding the same port with SO_REUSEPORT, so a connection is accepted, parsed, dispatched and answered on one thread with no hand-off or locks. Each HTTP/1.1 request or HTTP/2/3 stream runs as a stack-switched PHP coroutine with a per-connection arena reset between requests; parsing and framing stay in C (llhttp, nghttp2), and static files go out via sendfile with precompressed .br/.gz sidecars and an open-file cache without entering PHP. The benchmark handler is a trivial PHP closure run under OPcache JIT (opcache.jit=1255).
when_to_use: PHP services that want HTTP/2, HTTP/3, WebSocket, SSE and gRPC on one port from a single process, without php-fpm plus nginx in front.
Many small HTTP/2 responses with multiplexed streams (HttpArena baseline-h2c at 256 connections: 6.04M req/s vs 2.46M for the HttpArena nginx module, on a 64-core Threadripper PRO 3995WX).
Static-file serving over HTTP/2 with precompressed assets (static-h2 at 256 connections: 1.04M vs 0.80M req/s for nginx, same ~15 KB responses).
Memory-constrained hosts: about 0.2-0.5 GiB RSS on the HttpArena baseline and h2 profiles versus about 3.5 GiB for that nginx build.
Async PHP handlers that wait on databases or timers, since a waiting coroutine yields to the loop instead of holding a worker.
when_not_to_use: Plain HTTP/1.1 front-door or proxy duty: in the same suite it trails nginx on baseline-4096 (0.69x), pipelined (0.57x), limited-conn (0.68x), json-tls (0.60x) and json-h2c (about 0.71x).
When you need the fastest C or C++ HTTP/2 server: h2o (16.1M req/s) and agensio (14.7M) are about 3x faster on baseline-h2 at 256 connections in the same HttpArena data.

Stock PHP deployments: it requires the TrueAsync php-src fork (issue #6, run on stock PHP, is still open) plus OpenSSL 3.x, nghttp2 1.57+, and OpenSSL 3.5 / ngtcp2 / nghttp3 built from source for HTTP/3.
Windows multi-core serving: SO_REUSEPORT is Linux/BSD only, so on Windows workers > 1 give no parallelism (docs/USAGE.md caveats; closed issue #375).

Production users who need a stable API: 1,392 commits, 0.x releases roughly weekly, and the CHANGELOG keeps removing or rewiring config methods (twelve no-op HttpServerConfig setters now throw, #393).

integration.dependencies: TrueAsync PHP 8.6 fork with ext-async (libuv bundled), OpenSSL 3.0+ (3.5 for HTTP/3), libnghttp2 1.57+, optional libngtcp2 1.22+ and libnghttp3 1.15+, optional zlib-ng/zlib, brotli, zstd; llhttp 9.3.0 vendored
integration.min_toolchain: PHP 8.6 TrueAsync fork; phpize/configure build with a C compiler on Linux/macOS, PHP-SDK with MSVC on Windows
integration.platforms: Linux (full; HTTP/3 GSO and SO_REUSEPORT load balancing), macOS and BSD, Windows (single accept thread, no WebSocket build, lower HTTP/3 throughput)
integration.thread_safety: Each worker thread owns its own event loop and a deep-copied server object; handlers run as coroutines on that thread and share no mutable state unless you use the provided shared structures (rooms, cross-worker pub/sub, ThreadChannel).

gotchas: Harness flaw (cross-run, stale build): the TrueAsync rps lines in HttpArena's true-async-server.json have not changed since commit #1034 of 2026-07-24 (git blame), while nginx's rows come from the 2026-08-20 run (#1212); TrueAsync's h2 rows also lack the p99_latency field every other framework's h2 rows carry, so they were produced by an older harness version. The current Dockerfile image tag (0.7.0-rc.6) therefore does not identify the build that was measured.

Harness asymmetry (lighter responses): bytes per response derived from HttpArena's MiB/s bandwidth column are about 66 for TrueAsync vs 142 for nginx on HTTP/1.1, 21 vs 62 on h2c and 21 vs 86 on TLS h2 (nginx adds Server, Date, Connection and, on 8443, Alt-Svc). 66 bytes fits a response with no Date header, yet the server's own CHANGELOG added the RFC 9110 Date header to HTTP/1 in 0.7.0 (2026-06-01) and src/http1/http1_format.c now emits it on every response, so the HTTP/1.1 numbers were measured on code later changed for conformance.

The HTTP/2 path still emits no Date header: only src/http1/http1_format.c calls the Date formatter; nothing in src/http2 generates one, although RFC 9110 section 6.6.1 requires an origin server with a clock to send it on every protocol.

On kernels without load-balancing SO_REUSEPORT the shared-fd listener lets one worker take nearly every connection (open issue #329); HttpArena's frameworks/true-async-server/README.md is stale (names image 0.7.0-beta.5 and says baseline-h2c is not subscribed, while meta.json subscribes it and results exist).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Qbix Server or a php-fpm stack when the application code is PHP and you want HTTP/2/3, gRPC and WebSocket in-process; for a C or C++ server where raw HTTP/2 throughput matters, H2O is about 3x faster in the same HttpArena data, and for HTTP/1.1 nginx-class serving Kore, Lwan or Sogou Workflow are the better-documented choices.
verified_claims_summary: HttpArena (third-party suite, load generator on the same AMD Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-core host, Ubuntu 24.04, 5 s runs) shows TrueAsync Server with a trivial PHP handler at 6.04M req/s vs the HttpArena nginx 1.31.4 custom C module (-O3 -march=native) at 2.46M on baseline-h2c with 256 connections (2.46x), 1.60x at 1024 and 1.49x at 4096, 1.46x on TLS h2 at 256 and parity at 1024, and 1.29x on static-h2; it is slower than nginx on every HTTP/1.1 and JSON profile. The TrueAsync rows predate nginx's run by at least four weeks, come from an older harness version and, judging by HTTP/1.1 response sizes, a server build older than 0.7.0, and carry smaller responses (no Date or Server headers).
status_note: Very active single-maintainer project (last commit 2026-10-06, 0.16.0 released 2026-09-26, 72 stars), Apache-2.0 and usable today if you can run the TrueAsync PHP fork; expect API churn and evidence closer to C than B, since the HttpArena rows are cross-run and were measured on a build without the HTTP/1 Date header.
